body.statement: Let \(\tau(\Sigma)=N(\Sigma)/D(\Sigma)\) be an upstream-valid primitive coprime reduced rational causal certificate, obtained for example by the half-trek criterion, supported on \(S3\), with \(D\) nonzero, nonconstant, and homogeneous. Its denominator is exactly self-normalizing if and only if \(D=\lambda_0\Delta_1^a\Delta_2^b\delta^e\) for one nested flag and nonnegative integers \(a,b,e\) with positive sum. If the coefficients are rational, \(\mathcal A_D\) decides this property from the primitive input. Under Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}gaussian\text{-}sampling\), acceptance inherits Tamano's denominator-only identity \(D(\widehat\Sigma)/D(\Sigma)\stackrel{d}{=}\prod_{j=1}^{3}(\chi^2_{n-j+1}/n)^{m_j}\), where \(m=(a+b+e,b+e,e)\) and the factors are independent; consequently \(\Pr_\Sigma\{D(\Sigma)\in\mathcal I_D(\eta)\}=1-\eta\).
body.justification: This isolates the valid statistical payoff: exhaustive denominator classification plus Tamano's known exact pivot for the denominator value.
body.gap: Half-trek theory produces rational identifying functionals, while Tamano's Theorem 1 pivot applies to known flag powers; the new converse makes applicability decidable for every qualifying reduced three-variable denominator.
body.consumer: Analysts can attach an exact confidence set to \(D(\Sigma)\) while keeping inference for the causal ratio outside the claim.
